title: Continuous random variables
overview: Use probability density functions and integration to find probabilities, expectation and variance for continuous variables. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use the defining properties of a probability density function.
Find unknown constants by integrating total area to 1.
Calculate probabilities and percentiles by integration.

definitions.definition: A variable able to take any real value in an interval.
A non-negative function whose area over an interval gives probability and whose total area is 1.
Height per unit x; it can exceed 1 provided areas are valid probabilities.
A value m with equal probability on either side for a continuous distribution.
The interval on which the density is non-zero.

sections.title: Valid density functions
content: A pdf f(x) must satisfy f(x)≥0 on its support and ∫f(x)dx=1 over the whole support. Use normalisation to find unknown constants, checking they keep the density non-negative.
bullets: A density value is not itself a point probability.

examples.label: Key relationship
examples.content: Normalisation: ∫ f(x) dx=1 over the support

sections.title: Probabilities as areas
content: P(a < X < b)=∫ₐᵇf(x)dx after intersecting the requested interval with the support. For continuous X, endpoints make no difference: P(X=a)=0.
bullets: Draw the support and shade the required interval.

sections.title: Percentiles
content: A pth percentile q satisfies ∫ from the lower support limit to q of f(x)dx=p/100. The median uses 0.5. Solve and select the root that lies within the support.
bullets: Do not assume median equals mean unless symmetry justifies it.
Reject algebraic roots outside the support.

sections.title: Moments
content: Calculate E(X)=∫xf(x)dx and E(X²)=∫x²f(x)dx over the support, then Var(X)=E(X²)−[E(X)]². Interpret the mean in the same units as X and variance in squared units.
bullets: Keep exact values until the variance subtraction is complete.

examTips: Write the support beside every integral.
Check a final variance is non-negative and dimensionally sensible.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Integrating beyond the support without setting density to zero.
Accepting an algebraic root outside the allowed interval.

quickRecall.question: Can a pdf exceed 1?
quickRecall.answer: Yes; only areas must be between 0 and 1, and total area must equal 1.

quickRecall.question: What is P(X=a) for continuous X?
How is the median found?
quickRecall.answer: Set the area from the lower support boundary to m equal to 0.5.

quickRecall.question: Which root of a percentile equation is valid?
quickRecall.answer: Only a root lying in the stated support.
